scene_jp: <ruby>地下通路<rt>ちかつうろ</rt></ruby>への<ruby>入口<rt>いりぐち</rt></ruby>は、バーの<ruby>裏口<rt>うらぐち</rt></ruby>のさらに<ruby>奥<rt>おく</rt></ruby>にあった。<ruby>古<rt>ふる</rt></ruby>いコンクリートの<ruby>壁<rt>かべ</rt></ruby>に<ruby>沿<rt>そ</rt></ruby>って<ruby>歩<rt>ある</rt></ruby>いていくと、<ruby>空気<rt>くうき</rt></ruby>がひんやりと<ruby>変<rt>か</rt></ruby>わり、どこか<ruby>遠<rt>とお</rt></ruby>くで<ruby>水<rt>みず</rt></ruby>が<ruby>滴<rt>したた</rt></ruby>る<ruby>音<rt>おと</rt></ruby>がした。<ruby>薄暗<rt>うすぐら</rt></ruby>い<ruby>通路<rt>つうろ</rt></ruby>の<ruby>奥<rt>おく</rt></ruby>から、<ruby>灰色<rt>はいいろ</rt></ruby>のコートの<ruby>男<rt>おとこ</rt></ruby>の<ruby>声<rt>こえ</rt></ruby>が<ruby>聞<rt>き</rt></ruby>こえてきた。「<ruby>来<rt>き</rt></ruby>たか、テスト。この<ruby>先<rt>さき</rt></ruby>には、<ruby>君<rt>きみ</rt></ruby>の<ruby>祖母<rt>そぼ</rt></ruby>が<ruby>隠<rt>かく</rt></ruby>したものがあるはずだ。ただし、<ruby>進<rt>すす</rt></ruby>む<ruby>前<rt>まえ</rt></ruby>に<ruby>一<rt>ひと</rt></ruby>つだけ<ruby>聞<rt>き</rt></ruby>いておきたい。」<ruby>男<rt>おとこ</rt></ruby>は<ruby>立<rt>た</rt></ruby>ち<ruby>止<rt>ど</rt></ruby>まり、ゆっくりとこちらを<ruby>振<rt>ふ</rt></ruby>り<ruby>返<rt>かえ</rt></ruby>った。その<ruby>目<rt>め</rt></ruby>には、<ruby>追<rt>お</rt></ruby>いかけていた<ruby>頃<rt>ころ</rt></ruby>とは<ruby>違<rt>ちが</rt></ruby>う、<ruby>静<rt>しず</rt></ruby>かな<ruby>光<rt>ひかり</rt></ruby>があった。「<ruby>君<rt>きみ</rt></ruby>は、<ruby>祖母<rt>そぼ</rt></ruby>がなぜこのノートを<ruby>残<rt>のこ</rt></ruby>したと<ruby>思<rt>おも</rt></ruby>う？」
scene_translation: The entrance to the underground passage was tucked even deeper beyond the bar's back door. As you walked along the old concrete wall, the air turned cool and still, and somewhere in the distance came the faint sound of dripping water. From the dim depths of the passage, the voice of the man in the grey coat reached you. "So you came, Tesuto. Somewhere ahead lies what your grandmother hid — or so it should be. But before you go further, there is one thing I need to ask you." The man stopped and turned slowly to face you. In his eyes was a quiet light, different from the days when he had been following you. "Why do you think your grandmother left this notebook?"
grammar_note: 【はずだ】expresses the speaker's confident expectation based on reasoning — "it should be" / "it must be the case that." Here: 「<ruby>祖母<rt>そぼ</rt></ruby>が<ruby>隠<rt>かく</rt></ruby>したものがあるはずだ」= "There should be something your grandmother hid there." Attach to a plain-form verb or noun＋の: V-dictionary＋はずだ／V-た＋はずだ. It's different from でしょう (softer guess) — はずだ implies there is a logical basis for the belief.

vocab.meaning: cool and refreshing (of air or touch)
to turn around, to look back

mystery_memo: Scene 8: The man in grey (previously a follower, now revealed as a guide) has led the player into the wartime underground passage beneath Shinjuku. He knows the player's name and appears to have information about the grandmother. His question — why did the grandmother leave the notebook? — is the pivotal input prompt for this scene. The three clue fragments from NPCs (shopkeeper: the grandmother was afraid of someone; bartender: she made a map before she disappeared; shrine priest: she entrusted something sacred to the shrine) are converging. The coin locker key and the notebook's map both point to something hidden in this passage. The omamori from the shrine priest may have protective or unlocking significance deeper in. The blue woman's identity as the grandmother's former student has not yet been directly confronted.
